claim: Aponiente's 2026 tasting menu is priced at 400 euros per person, with optional drink pairings: NoLo 180 euros, Albariza 210 euros, Diatoms 330 euros (VAT included).
quote: MENU APONIENTE 2026 400 E individual (official menu PDF; pairings NoLo 180, Albariza 210, Diatoms 330, IVA incluido)

claim: Aponiente takes reservations via its website booking system, phone 956 851 870 / 606 225 859, or email reservas@aponiente.com, and located at C/ Francisco Cossi Ochoa s/n.
quote: 956 851 870 – 606 225 859 ... reservas@aponiente.com ... C/ Francisco Cossi Ochoa, s/n El Puerto de Santa María, Cádiz

claim: For the 2026 season Aponiente serves part of the meal outdoors in the marshes around the tide mill via walkways over the water, with a kitchen set in the estero landscape; the season had opened by early May 2026.
quote: Part of the meal is now served outdoors in the marshes around the tide mill, with walkways over the water, a kitchen in the estero landscape ... radically innovative, but also deeply local

claim: Aponiente, run by Ángel León 'Chef of the Sea', occupies a converted 19th-century tide mill and is celebrated for sea-based cuisine respecting the ecosystem.
quote: Ángel León, known as 'The Chef of the Sea', has transformed this old tide mill into the epicentre of an exceptional gastronomic experience

claim: Reservations at Aponiente should be made well in advance as tables are limited, with seatings for lunch (roughly 13:00-14:15) and dinner (roughly 20:00-21:15).
quote: tables are limited during specific time slots for lunch (1–2:15) and dinner (8–9:15)

claim: La Taberna del Chef del Mar, Ángel León's casual venue in central El Puerto on the site where Aponiente earned its first two stars, serves shareable tapas/raciones (rice with plankton, squid croquettes and tartare, flame-grilled tuna, octopus skewers).
quote: located in the very heart of El Puerto de Santa María at the same place where Ángel León and his crew achieved 2 Michelin stars for Aponiente ... rice with plankton, squid croquettes and squid tartare ... flame-grilled tuna steak and octopus skewers

claim: La Taberna del Chef del Mar dishes run roughly 5-25 euros a la carte with fixed menus around 45 and 55 euros, in a casual friendly atmosphere.
quote: average prices ranging from 5€ to 25€ ... fixed menus at 45 and 55 euros ... casual and friendly spot

claim: Romerijo is a 70-plus-year El Puerto institution (since 1952) on the Ribera del Marisco where customers buy cooked and fried seafood by weight from 30+ specialties and eat on the terrace.
quote: más de 60 años de historia ... dedicada a la compra, manipulación, elaboración y venta de marisco y pescado ... compran al peso de más de 30 especialidades

claim: Mantúa (Israel Ramos) and LU Cocina y Alma (JuanLu Fernández) are one-Michelin-star restaurants located in neighbouring Jerez de la Frontera, not in El Puerto itself.
quote: Mantúa is a One Star Michelin restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide España ... The restaurant is located in Jerez de la Frontera, not El Puerto de Santa María

claim: Castillo de San Marcos is a 13th-century fortress now owned by Bodegas Caballero; visits combine castle history with a Jerez wine tasting, open 10:00-16:00 Sept-June (10:00-20:00 July-Aug), with guided tours Tue-Fri at 13:00 and Sat at 11:00 and 13:00, costing roughly 8-14 for castle visits and 14-20 for the castle-plus-winery tasting.
quote: Castle + winery with wine tasting | 2 hours | 14-20 | ... discover a wonderful historic winery ... three excellent Jerez wines, a Lustau vermouth and the famous Ponche Caballero. Tuesday-Friday: 1:00 PM tour; Saturdays: 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM tours

claim: The Castillo de San Marcos was built over a former mosque by King Alfonso X the Wise after the Reconquest, layering Moorish and Christian heritage in the heart of the old town.
quote: a 13th-century fortress built over a former mosque by King Alfonso X the Wise following the taking of the town during the Reconquest

claim: El Puerto's Plaza Real de Toros, one of Spain's largest and most prestigious bullrings, can be visited Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 and 17:00-19:00 and Sat 10:00-14:00, with guided visits 6 and self-guided 4.
quote: open Tuesday to Friday from 10:00 to 14:00 and 17:00 to 19:00, and Saturday from 10:00 to 14:00 ... Guided visits cost 6, and self-guided visits cost 4 ... managed by the company Serlo S.L.

claim: Visitors warn the Plaza de Toros has sometimes been found closed during its posted opening hours despite advance confirmation, so calling ahead is advisable.
quote: the bullring has been closed during posted opening hours despite advance confirmation with the tourist office, so it's advisable to confirm hours before your visit

claim: The Fundación Rafael Alberti, the poet's childhood home on Calle Santo Domingo 25, opens Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 and Sat-Sun 11:00-14:00; general admission is 4 (2 students/pensioners, free for El Puerto residents).
quote: abierto de martes a viernes de 10:00 a 14:00 horas, y los sabados y domingos de 11:00 a 14:00 horas ... La entrada general cuesta 4, estudiantes y pensionistas 2 ... gratuito para nacidos o residentes en El Puerto de Santa Maria

claim: The Iglesia Mayor Prioral, a minor basilica documented from 1486 and promoted by the Dukes of Medinaceli, dominates the old-town square as the city's principal church.
quote: Its construction is documented from 1486, coinciding with the construction boom promoted by the Dukes of Medinaceli, who were the jurisdictional lords of the town

claim: The Iglesia Mayor Prioral is under restoration into early 2026 with scaffolding on the facade, but access through the Puerta del Sol stays open and worship continues uninterrupted.
quote: despite the scaffolding covering the facade, access to the temple through the Puerta del Sol will remain open at all times, and religious worship and liturgical activities will not be interrupted

claim: The Monasterio de la Victoria, a former Minim monastery now declared Bien de Interes Cultural and used for concerts and exhibitions, can be visited Mondays and Fridays (except holidays) 11:00-14:00, with a tour of the church, cloister and chapter halls plus an 11-minute introductory video.
quote: abierto todos los lunes y viernes (excepto festivos) entre las 11:00 y las 14:00 horas ... podra contemplar la iglesia, el claustro y las salas capitulares ... un video introductorio de alrededor de 11 minutos

claim: The Museo Municipal at Calle Pagador 1 has free admission and opens Tue-Fri 10:00-14:00 and Sat/Sun/holidays 11:00-14:00, housing the city's archaeological and fine-arts collections.
quote: Tuesday to Friday: 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.; Saturday, Sunday and holidays: 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. ... Admission is free ... C/ Pagador, n 1

claim: El Puerto's nickname 'City of the Hundred Palaces' comes from the 17th-18th-century casas-palacio of the cargadores a Indias, three-storey merchant mansions built around porticoed patios and crowned with mirador watchtowers; landmark examples are the 1660 Palacio de Aranibar (the oldest) and the Casa-Palacio de Vizarron (de las Cadenas), which hosted Felipe V and Isabel de Farnesio in 1729-1730.
quote: the city of the Cien Palacios (Hundred Palaces) ... structured in three floors ... watchtower or mirador tower ... Palacio de Aranibar, built in 1660, considered the oldest house of cargadores a Indias ... Casa-Palacio de Vizarron or of the Chains, which in 1729 and 1730 hosted the Spanish kings Felipe V and Isabel de Farnesio

claim: In April 2026 the Guadalete riverfront gained a new draw with the opening of La Ribera, a gastronomic market on Avenida de la Bajamar at the catamaran terminal combining food stalls, terraces and leisure programming.
quote: the Guadalete riverfront area gained a new focus of activity with the opening of La Ribera, a gastronomic market located on Avenida de la Bajamar at the catamaran terminal

claim: El Puerto is transforming its Guadalete riverfront into a paseo fluvial of six promenades and plazas with green areas and event spaces, and a second pedestrian footbridge over the river was due for completion in early 2026.
quote: six promenades and plazas ... public spaces for events and cultural activities, along with new green areas and recreational zones ... A second pedestrian footbridge over the Guadalete River is expected to be completed by February or March 2026

claim: El Puerto de Santa María is one of three Sherry Triangle towns with Jerez and Sanlúcar; its tidal-river bodegas give Finos a distinctive salty taste, sold as Puerto Fino.
quote: Since dry Sherries (or Finos) age in contact with the air, the location of the bodegas, right next to a tidal river, gives Finos from el Puerto a very distinctive and slightly salty taste.

claim: Before the Cádiz rail link, all Jerez sherry was stored in El Puerto warehouses before shipping worldwide; local styles include fino (driest, palest), amontillado and oloroso, while manzanilla is exclusive to Sanlúcar.
quote: all the sherry from Jerez was stored in warehouses at Santa Maria before being shipped all over the world

claim: Bodegas Osborne in El Puerto offers a fortified-wine tasting at 12€, a brandy tasting at 15€ and a VORS tasting at 35€ per person, plus a Toro Gallery stroll with four sherries and Cinco Jotas Iberian ham.
quote: Fortified wine tasting: 12€ (per person), Brandy tasting: 15€ (per person), and VORS tasting: 35€ (per person)

claim: Osborne's El Puerto cellar is the oldest aging bodega in the Jerez region, producing Quinta fino, Coquinero amontillado, Bailén and Sibarita oloroso, and Pedro Ximénez 1827, with tastings, a shop and visits at Calle Los Moros 7.
quote: la bodega de envejecimiento más antigua del marco de Jerez

claim: Bodegas Gutiérrez Colosía, founded 1838 and the only riverside winery on the Guadalete by the Cádiz ferry, runs 1.5-hour tours ending in a six-wine tasting, with English at 11.15am and Spanish at 12.30pm Mon-Fri.
quote: Tours last 1½ hours and end with a six-wine tasting, which can include tapas and flamenco on request, and run at 11.15am in English and 12.30pm in Spanish Monday to Friday

claim: Bodegas Grant (Juan C. Grant, est. 1841, aka Las 7 Esquinas) is a family producer of Puerto Fino by the criaderas-and-soleras method, with a traditional tasting patio; visits are Saturdays by prior appointment.
quote: Visits are possible on Saturday with previous appointment.

claim: Bodegas 501 (Carlos & Javier de Terry) is a historic El Puerto brandy house behind Brandy 501, but it ceased winery activity to become a distributor and since 2009 its 501 range is produced by Grupo Osborne.
quote: In 2009, a major agreement was reached with Grupo Osborne, by which Osborne would undertake to produce the 501 brandy range in its three varieties for the national market.

claim: In 2026 El Puerto de Santa María holds Blue Flags on four beaches (Fuentebravía, La Puntilla, Santa Catalina/Vistahermosa-Las Redes, Valdelagrana) plus Puerto Sherry marina.
quote: criterios como la calidad del agua, la gestión ambiental, la accesibilidad o los servicios disponibles

claim: Valdelagrana is an urban Blue Flag beach 1,880m long and 85m wide with hammock rentals, food and a children's zone; La Puntilla is 1,300m with surf; Fuentebravía 700m semi-urban with surf/diving; Santa Catalina (Vistahermosa) 3,000m long; La Calita is the smallest at 590m with diving.
quote: Valdelagrana ... 85 metros ... 1.880 metros ... Bandera azul

claim: Playa La Puntilla sits at the mouth of the Guadalete river, separated from it by a breakwater, with calm bathing waters, accessibility for reduced mobility and over 100 parking spaces.
quote: La Puntilla ... desembocadura del río Guadalete ... aguas tranquilas para el baño

claim: Playa La Calita has a wild appearance with rocky outcrops in the water and sand, making it good for spearfishing and scuba diving, and does not hold a Blue Flag.
quote: aspecto salvaje ... rocas ... ideal para la pesca submarina y el buceo

claim: Puerto Sherry is a marina and yacht club in the Bay of Cádiz offering moorings, boat rentals and waterfront facilities, a hub for nautical activity.
quote: Puerto Sherry | Marina & Yacht Club in El Puerto de Santa María

claim: Private boat trips depart Puerto Sherry's dock M with an accredited skipper, sailing to Valdelagrana to anchor, swim and do paddle surf on a roughly three-hour outing.
quote: Meeting at dock M in Puerto Sherry ... sailing to Valdelagrana beach where you can drop anchor ... paddle surfing and water sports

claim: The Sendero Pinar de la Algaida is a 12km round-trip walk through stone-pine forest and marshland skirting a saltpan, best done September to May at low tide with binoculars for birds.
quote: 12km ... Pinar de la Algaida, a forest of stone pines ... best time to walk is from September to May, at low tide

claim: Bahía de Cádiz Natural Park spans ~10,522 hectares across five municipalities including El Puerto de Santa María, with the untouched Pinar del Coto de la Isleta pine forest, salt flats and mudflats hosting over 50,000 aquatic birds including flamingos, spoonbills, terns and avocets.
quote: populations of more than 50,000 aquatic birds, with flamingos among the notable species

claim: Romerijo on Ribera del Marisco is a 70-year-old institution with separate cocedero (boiled) and freiduría (fried) counters where you pick seafood served in paper cones (papelón/cucurucho) to eat at tables or take away.
quote: Romerijo has played a pivotal role in the commercial development of La Ribera del Marisco, the city's most popular gastronomic district. Guests select the fresh products they wish to enjoy at the cooking station, which are then served in their signature paper cones.

claim: At Romerijo order gamba blanca gorda, langostino de Sanlúcar, cañaíllas and quisquillas at the counter; nearby La Venancia (Plaza de las Galeras Reales) is a classic Andalusian tavern for varied pescaíto frito (acedías, boquerones, puntillitas) and pastel de corvina.
quote: Romerijo — Specialties: Gamba blanca gorda, langostino de Sanlúcar, cañaíllas, quisquillas... La Venancia — Must-try: Pastel de corvina, varied pescaíto frito (acedías, boquerones, puntillitas). Classic Andalusian tavern.

claim: El Puerto's seafood spread covers bocas, nécoras, percebes, camarones, cañaíllas, cigalas and langostinos; pescaíto frito perfumes the streets, and a signature local dish is caldillo de perro made with fresh hake; the tapas route runs along Calle Misericordia, Ribera del Marisco and the promenade.
quote: pescaíto frito que impregnan de un olor característico las calles del municipio. A signature dish is caldillo de perro, made with fresh large hake... tapas route through bars on Calle Misericordia, the Ribera del Marisco waterfront area, and the maritime promenade.

claim: Atún rojo de almadraba is an El Puerto specialty best from April to June; Tritón Gastrobar (C. Ribera del Marisco 6) serves red-tuna tataki, marinated tacos and tartare with avocado and seaweed chips.
quote: red tuna from almadraba (a traditional fishing method). The optimal season... is April-June... Tritón Gastrobar... Red tuna tataki with soy sauce and ginger; Red tuna marinaded tacos; Red tuna tartare with avocado and seaweed chips.

claim: Bodegas Obregón is an authentic central El Puerto tabanco serving sherry (Fino, Amontillado, Oloroso) poured straight from the barrel with weekend hot tapas like chicken cooked in Pedro Ximénez (~€5.50); cash-only, crowded, locals-heavy.
quote: serves sherry and other wines directly from wooden barrels... On weekends, they offer hot tapas and traditional Cadiz dishes. One reviewer noted it serves chicken cooked in Pedro Ximenez (sweet sherry) for around €5.50... bring cash.

claim: Toro Tapas, set within the Bodegas Osborne wine-tourism complex, is a top-rated El Puerto tapas spot (user rating 9.3) for dishes like tortillitas de camarones and pescaíto frito (~€25-35 pp).
quote: Toro Tapas with a rating of 9.3... a renowned restaurant located within the Bodegas Osborne Wine Tourism complex... high-quality and challenging cuisine.

claim: Jerez (XRY) is the closest airport at a 30-minute drive via the A4; the C-1 line links El Puerto to Cadiz (35 min, EUR 3.90) and Jerez (10 min); 3 daily direct Alvia trains run from Madrid Atocha.
quote: Jerez (XRY) is the closest option, 30-minute drive via the A4... The C-1 line connects El Puerto to Cadiz (35 minutes, EUR3.90) and Jerez (10 minutes). 3 daily Alvia trains direct to Cadiz run from Madrid's Atocha station

claim: The El Vapor catamaran crossing takes roughly 30-40 minutes, departs from the riverside El Vapor terminal in El Puerto and docks at Muelle Ciudad in central Cadiz; the Consorcio de Transportes de la Bahia de Cadiz operates it.
quote: Crossing Time: approximately 30-40 minutes... terminal is located at the riverside... known as 'El Vapor'... Ferries dock at 'Muelle Ciudad,' positioning passengers directly in Cadiz's historic center... Consorcio de Transportes de la Bahia de Cadiz operates the service

claim: El Puerto forms one corner of the Sherry Triangle with Jerez and Sanlucar; the catamaran from the harbour by Plaza de San Juan crosses to Cadiz in about 20 minutes for EUR 2.80 each way, and Jerez is a 20-minute drive.
quote: the great sherry triangle that connects with Jerez de la Frontera and Sanlucar de Barrameda... take the catamaran ferry from the harbor in front of Plaza de San Juan. The frequent, 20-minute crossing costs 2.80EUR each way... Jerez de la Frontera. It is a 20-minute drive

claim: The Feria de Primavera y Fiesta del Vino Fino (Spring Fair) 2026 runs April 29 to May 4 on the Las Banderas fairground, with every fair-tent open to the public unlike Seville or Cordoba.
quote: La Feria de El Puerto de Santa Maria 2026 takes place from April 29 to May 4... the huge Las Banderas fairground becomes filled with fair-tents... Unlike the more exclusive fairs of Seville or Cordoba, every single tent here is open to the public

claim: Semana Santa (Holy Week) processions in El Puerto in 2026 begin on Palm Sunday, March 29.
quote: Holy Week processions are scheduled to begin on Palm Sunday, March 29, 2026

claim: The Crisol Monasterio de San Miguel hotel occupies a baroque 1727 convent built for the Capuchin Poor Clares by the Duke of Medinaceli, with 164 rooms close to the beach, shops and monuments.
quote: Monasterio San Miguel, a gracious baroque building and converted convent which dates back to 1727... built by order of the Duke of Medinaceli to house the Clarisas Capuchinas nuns... 164 sober and elegant rooms... close to the beach, the main shopping streets

claim: Hotel Puerto Sherry is a 60-room nautical-themed waterfront hotel beside the Puerto Sherry marina just outside town, with a rooftop terrace and seasonal outdoor pool.
quote: nautical-themed hotel is located in Puerto Sherry, just outside of El Puerto de Santa Maria, near the marina... rooftop terrace and seasonal outdoor pool... 60 rooms

claim: Jerez is famous for sherry, flamenco and Carthusian horses; the Royal Andalusian School of Equestrian Art runs its 'How the Andalusian Horses Dance' show midday on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and the Feria del Caballo runs 9-16 May 2026.
quote: Jerez is famous for three things: sherry wine, flamenco, and Carthusian horses... the famous show 'How the Andalusian Horses Dance,' available midday on Tuesdays & Thursdays... The Feria del Caballo runs 9-16 May 2026

claim: From Seville Airport travellers take the EA bus to Santa Justa station then a direct Renfe train to El Puerto (roughly 55 minutes total via Cercanias/MD), with fares from about EUR 9-18 one way.
quote: hop on the EA airport bus to Santa Justa station, then take the Cercanias C-1 train... El Puerto de Santa Maria around 55 minutes... direct train to El Porto... cost is around 18EUR one way

claim: Sanlúcar de Barrameda sits roughly 27 km from El Puerto de Santa María, about a 30-minute drive.
quote: It's 17 miles or 27 km from Sanlucar de Barrameda to El Puerto de Santa Maria ... It takes about 30 minutes to drive between the two cities.

claim: Bodegas Barbadillo, which first bottled manzanilla in 1827, offers tourist tours from a €5 museum visit with one glass to a €20 two-centuries-of-history tour with a three-wine tasting.
quote: The Barbadillo family settled in Sanlucar de Barrameda and bottled Manzanilla for the first time in 1827 ... museum guided tour + tasting of 1 glass of Manzanilla (€5 ... a tasting of 3 emblematic wines (Adults: 20€

claim: Family-owned Bodegas Hidalgo, founded 1792, still makes La Gitana manzanilla and runs central two-hour tours plus specialised sunset (€40) and summer night (€35) tastings.
quote: family-owned 1792-founded Bodegas Hidalgo still produces the famed La Gitana manzanillas ... specialised visits include sunset tastings among the vines (€40) and summer night tours (€35)

claim: Casa Bigote, founded 1951 in the Bajo de Guía fishing quarter at the Guadalquivir's mouth, is famed for its langostinos and seafood with views over Doñana.
quote: Casa Bigote is located in Bajo de Guía at the mouth of the Guadalquivir River with views of Doñana ... founded in 1951 ... renowned for its fresh seafood, particularly the langostinos

claim: Casa Bigote took a temporary closure through the end of March 2026, reopening reservations from 23 March 2026.
quote: Casa Bigote, situated in Bajo de Guía ... announced a temporary closure for vacation until the end of March 2026 ... reservations reopen starting March 23, 2026.

claim: Doñana boat trips aboard the riverboat Real Fernando depart from Bajo de Guía to Poblado de la Plancha in the national park; the round trip runs 3.5 hours costing €30 adults and €20 children.
quote: aboard the riverboat Royal Fernando ... begins in Sanlúcar de Barrameda ... from the location known as Bajo Guía ... The round trip takes 3½ hours and tickets cost 30€ for adults and 20€ for children

claim: The Sanlúcar beach horse races run on two sets of August 2026 dates (Aug 8-10 and Aug 21-23) at evening low tide, are among Europe's oldest equestrian events, and were declared of International Tourist Interest in 1997.
quote: Dates: August 8-10 and August 21-23, 2026 ... the oldest equestrian activities in Spain and one of the oldest ones in Europe ... declared of International Tourist Interest in 1997.
